extracted.intended_audience: attorneys, in-house counsel, trade associations, and stakeholders who draft notice-and-comment letters on agency rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting effective notice-and-comment letters responding to agency proposed rules, focusing on making submissions useful to agency staff and likely to influence final regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address the actual proposed rule text
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure your comments address the proposed rule text, which is the most important part of the proposal as it has the potential to become regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus critique and suggestions on the specific regulatory text the agency has proposed (not only high-level complaints). Targeting the proposed text increases the chance the agency can incorporate changes into final regulations. Avoid exclusively abstract or non-textual objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with the preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the preamble that precedes the proposed rule text. The preamble explains the agency's rationale and reveals which arguments will resonate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the preamble to understand the agency's reasoning, stated goals, and evidence; tailor comments to counter or reinforce those rationales. Cite or quote relevant preamble passages to show why your point addresses the agency's expressed concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference specific sections
rubrics_metrics.description: An effective comment letter should refer to particular sections of the proposal, including specific proposed regulatory text and relevant statutes to make it easy for staff to categorize comments with others on the same topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include precise citations (section numbers, paragraph identifiers, statutory citations). Clear section-level referencing helps agency staff group and synthesize comments and increases the likelihood your point will be tracked and considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep it focused
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the letter focused and not overly verbose, remembering that staff will review many letters, and the easier it is to lift something from your letter, the more effective it will be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concise, use clear organization (headings, summaries), and prioritize the strongest arguments. Long, sprawling, or unfocused submissions reduce the chance staff will find and use your recommendations. Make it easy for reviewers to extract key text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow critiques with alternative solutions—any criticism of a proposed rule should be followed with an appropriate alternative solution, providing specific amendments to the language if you oppose particular rule text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When objecting to language, include concrete replacements (redline, proposed regulatory text, or specific amendments). Providing ready edits or workable options increases persuasiveness and the likelihood of agency adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet the deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Meet the Federal Register deadline for comments submissions, which is usually 30 to 90 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify the exact comment deadline in the notice and submit on time; late filings are less likely to be considered. Plan internal review and clearance timelines to ensure timely submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make staff's job easier
rubrics_metrics.description: Make staff's job easier (via clear organization, specific section citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize comments logically, use headings or an executive summary, and pinpoint the exact text you address. The more readily staff can identify, categorize, and lift your points, the more useful your submission will be.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide ready-to-adopt regulatory language alternatives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply draft text that staff can insert or adapt, including specific amendments, regulatory language, or redlines. Ready-to-use language is more actionable than abstract recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame arguments in terms the agency can use in its preamble response
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame arguments in terms the agency can use in its preamble response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the agency's terminology, statutory framework, policy rationales, and analytical structures (e.g., cost-benefit considerations) so the agency can directly rely on your points when explaining decisions in the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overly broad or political framings
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid overly broad or political framings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep comments focused on legal, technical, and policy considerations relevant to the rulemaking rather than partisan or political messaging, which is less likely to persuade agency staff or be incorporated into regulatory reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function as a drafting aid for the agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective comment letters function as drafting aids for the agency, providing specific text that can be incorporated or used as a basis for the agency's reasoning in the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position submissions to solve drafting problems—explain how proposed wording addresses issues, show alignment with statutes, and provide clear, implementable text. Think of comments as practical tools that translate critique into workable regulatory solutions.
